title: No Slides

pre.en: Why did Chen give his talk without slides?
pre.zh: 小陈为什么最后没用幻灯片？
options: Rachel told him not to use them.
The CEO had already banned slides.

intro: 一个「临时上台」的小故事：小陈被临时叫去给全公司做英语报告，偏偏关键时刻电脑出了问题。读的时候留意 although、even though 和 however：前两个把相反的两件事放在同一句里，however 则另起一句来转折；也想想没有幻灯片时，什么样的讲法最能打动人。

sentences.en: On Wednesday evening, Rachel asked Chen to give a presentation to the whole company — in English.
sentences.zh: 周三晚上，Rachel 让小陈给全公司做一场报告——还得用英语。

sentences.en: The person who was supposed to speak had cancelled, so she needed someone at short notice.
sentences.zh: 原本要讲的人临时来不了了，她得临时找个人顶上。

sentences.en: "I'd rather fix ten bugs than give a talk," said Chen.
sentences.zh: 「我宁可去修十个 bug，也不想上台讲，」小陈说。

sentences.en: He wanted to turn it down.
sentences.zh: 他想推掉。

sentences.en: However, nobody says no to Rachel.
sentences.zh: 可是，谁也没法对 Rachel 说不。

sentences.en: Although he was exhausted after a long day, he worked on his slides until two in the morning.
sentences.zh: 虽然忙了一整天已经累坏了，他还是做幻灯片做到了凌晨两点。

sentences.en: He made forty slides and threw away half of them.
sentences.zh: 他做了四十页，又删掉了一半。

sentences.en: Rachel signed off on the rest over breakfast, although she said they were still a bit long.
sentences.zh: Rachel 边吃早饭边批了剩下的，不过她说还是有点长。

sentences.en: At ten o'clock, the room was so packed that people were standing at the back.
sentences.zh: 十点钟，会议室挤得满满当当，后面的人只能站着。

sentences.en: "Right, let's get started," said the CEO, and Chen walked to the front.
sentences.zh: 「好，我们开始吧，」CEO 话音刚落，小陈走到了前面。

sentences.en: He was about to begin when his laptop died.
sentences.zh: 他刚要开口，笔记本电脑突然黑屏了。

sentences.en: While he was trying to restart it, the room went quiet, and his mind went blank.
sentences.zh: 他正忙着重启，会场一下子安静了，他的脑子一片空白。

sentences.en: He had no idea how to give a talk without slides.
sentences.zh: 没有幻灯片，他完全不知道该怎么讲。

sentences.en: He tried not to panic.
sentences.zh: 他努力让自己别慌。

sentences.en: So he decided to keep it simple and just tell them a story.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定简单点，就给大家讲个故事。

sentences.en: He told them about an eighty-year-old user who'd emailed the team.
sentences.zh: 他讲了一位八十岁的用户，她给团队发过一封邮件。

sentences.en: Thanks to their app, she could finally video-call her grandson in Canada.
sentences.zh: 多亏了他们的 App，她终于能和远在加拿大的孙子视频通话了。

sentences.en: Even though his voice was shaking at first, the audience listened.
sentences.zh: 虽然一开始他的声音在发抖，大家还是认真听着。

sentences.en: He spoke up so that the people at the back could hear.
sentences.zh: 他提高了嗓门，好让后排的人也听得见。

sentences.en: And slowly, he got his message across.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，他把想说的都讲清楚了。

sentences.en: Afterwards, the CEO came over.
sentences.zh: 结束后，CEO 走了过来。

sentences.en: He was the man who'd got lost with Chen on his first day in London.
sentences.zh: 就是小陈第一天到伦敦时，跟他一起迷路的那位。

sentences.en: "That was the best presentation of the year," he said.
sentences.zh: 「这是今年最好的一场报告，」他说。

sentences.en: Then he banned slides for a month.
sentences.zh: 接着，他宣布一个月内禁用幻灯片。

cards.note: to talk to a group of people about a subject, often using slides
cards.tip: 动词最常用 give，正式一点用 make，口语里也说 do a presentation；换个说法是 give a talk。
cards.example: I have to give a presentation to the client on Monday.

cards.note: with very little warning or time to prepare
cards.tip: 英式说法，美式多说 on short notice；道歉时常加 such：Sorry to ask at such short notice。
cards.example: Thanks for joining the call at such short notice.

cards.note: used to say what you would prefer to do
to say no to a request or an offer
to spend time doing, making or improving something
to get rid of something you don't want, usually by putting it in the bin
to give official approval to something
口语常说 The train was packed.；意思接近 crowded，但更夸张。
to begin doing something
cards.tip: 开会、上课开场最常用的一句就是 Let's get started.；比 Let's start 更自然。
cards.example: Shall we get started? Everyone's here.

cards.note: to be going to happen or do something very soon
cards.tip: 常和 when 连用，说「正要…的时候，突然…」：I was about to leave when it started to rain.
cards.example: I was about to call you.

cards.note: to become silent
if your mind goes blank, you suddenly cannot remember or think of anything
cards.tip: 主语多是 mind；屏幕也能 go blank（黑屏）。go 在这里是「变得」，同类说法有 go quiet、go red。
cards.example: When the interviewer asked my first question, my mind went blank.

cards.note: to not know something at all
cards.tip: 后面可以直接接 how / what / where 从句（陈述语序），也可以接 that 从句。
cards.example: I had no idea the meeting was cancelled.

cards.note: to do something in a simple way, without too many details
cards.tip: it 不指具体的东西，是固定说法；工程师常说的 KISS 原则就是 Keep it simple, stupid。
cards.example: Keep it simple — one screen, one button.

cards.note: 后面接名词，多说好的原因；也能带点讽刺说坏结果：Thanks to the traffic, I was late.
过去式 shook，过去分词 shaken；紧张时常说 My hands were shaking.
指全体听众，是一个整体；说其中一个人用 a member of the audience。
to speak more loudly so that people can hear you
cards.tip: 还有「站出来说话、发表意见」的意思：Don't be afraid to speak up in meetings。
cards.example: Could you speak up a bit? The line is bad.

cards.zh: 把意思讲清楚；让人听明白
cards.note: to make people understand what you want to tell them
cards.tip: your 随主语变：get his / her / our message across；across 不能丢。
cards.example: Short sentences help you get your message across.

cards.note: 英式常用 afterwards，美式多说 afterward；放句首、句末都可以。
to come to the place where someone is, especially their home
to become unable to find your way
ban sth / ban sb from doing sth；过去式 banned 要双写 n。名词 a ban on sth。
